A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALEXR algorithm and cFCCO research. Their main text, appendices, equations, figures and tables are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V4 Section 9 reports original GDRO and pAUC experiments, including validation curves and test results. Appendix F provides additional empirical analyses.

after.justification: V5 Section 5 retains original GDRO accuracy results and GDRO/pAUC validation curves. Appendix G retains empirical group-population and dual-radius analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same block sampling, extrapolated inner-function estimator, dual mirror update and stochastic primal proximal update. The main ALEXR procedure and its primal-only implementation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GDRO on Adult and CelebA with the same constructed groups, and pAUC on Covtype, Higgs, Cardiomegaly and Lung-mass with TPR thresholds 0.5 and 0.75. Changes concern settings and partitions within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: OOA disappears from the GDRO loss curves but remains in the accuracy table. The pAUC displays no longer report OOA or CE results. SONX is replaced by the MSVR label and a subgradient-adaptation description, but identical overlapping GDRO values leave a rerun versus relabeling unresolved.

E3.justification: V4 specifies Covtype train/validation/test splits of 60/20/20 and separate 500,000-example Higgs validation and test sets. V5 describes 75/25 Covtype splitting and Higgs validation with the remainder for training. Its appendix retains the old training/validation counts, so actual reassignment is unclear. GDRO drops alpha=0.2 and 0.25, and the SOX momentum-search grid narrows from five values to three.

E4.justification: V4 Appendix H's theoretical ablation of theta=0 is removed. It tested the role of extrapolation through bounds for both convex regimes and identified losses in deterministic convergence and parallel speedup. The group-population and dual-radius analyses in Figure 3 are retained.

E5.justification: V5 omits the explicit five-run, different-random-seed specification for pAUC given in v4 Appendix F.2.2. GDRO retains five-run reporting and the same corresponding plus/minus entries. The omission does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: V5 removes the entire pAUC test-results table, the pAUC loss curves, and GDRO results for alpha=0.2 and 0.25. Common GDRO accuracy entries are identical, including the SONX/MSVR-labeled row. V5 Table 2 adds means across four retained settings, including 66.80 for ALEXR; this is not a demonstrated performance improvement.

T1.justification: V4's regularization-conversion theorem, baseline-reduction derivations and theta=0 convergence theorems are removed. V5 Appendix D.1.2 revises the strongly convex telescoping argument and its tau parameter relation. V5 Theorem 2 omits v4's explicit smooth-mirror-function condition, although Appendix D.2 still requires it. Most principal rates are retained and reexpressed as oracle complexities.

C1.justification: V5 qualifies the optimality claim as near-optimality in the title, abstract and conclusion. The central contributions—single-loop ALEXR, improved convergence bounds and lower bounds for cFCCO—remain.

C2.justification: V5 explicitly emphasizes that strong convexity cannot improve the rate when the outer function is nonsmooth. It removes v4's prominent explanation of the smooth-mirror restriction and the associated limitation on choosing the outer conjugate. The GDRO outlier rationale and sparsity interpretation remain.

D1.justification: V5 drops the pAUC tuning recipe, explicit per-dataset iteration budgets and Adult/CelebA split-size descriptions. PyTorch, workstation specifications, feature preprocessing and the OOA projection implementation were already documented in v4 and remain available in v5.

R1.justification: The relationship to SCO changes substantially: v4 Section 3.2 and Appendix G.1 describe applying SCO algorithms to FCCO with O(n) oracle costs, whereas v5 declares them inapplicable and removes those reductions. The deterministic saddle-point survey is substantially reduced, while references on subgroup fairness and potential-function proofs are added.

P1.justification: V5 extensively rewrites and condenses the introduction and theoretical narrative. Preliminaries, algorithm and convergence analysis are consolidated into Section 3; applications move into the experiments and Appendix B, and GDRO theory moves to Appendix F. These are substantial structural changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V5 adopts a two-column main text, restructures the complexity comparisons and adds a notation table. Figure 1 shrinks from eight panels to four; Figure 2 drops its loss panels and rearranges the pAUC panels. Training-curve axes change from iterations to oracle counts, and the pAUC test-results table disappears.

improvement.justification: V5 offers clearer organization, more cautious optimality wording and local proof corrections. However, removing the pAUC test evaluation and extrapolation ablation weakens supporting evidence. Unreconciled split descriptions and omission of a theorem condition still required by its proof reduce precision. These losses outweigh the presentation gains, while the core method and principal rates remain.
